asks: How long have you got? I ask everyone.
Do you know how deep this room goes?
Would you cut your name in? Most people do.
description: The wall is bark: deep-fissured, warm, running up past where the ceiling should be and going on. Sap has dried in the cracks in long amber runs.
emotes: {it} creaks the way a mast creaks, high up, out of sight.
Something small runs up {it} and disappears into a crack.
A slow bead of sap works its way down {it} and stops, thinking about it.
{it} shifts a fraction, and every hanging thing in the room swings.
looks: The fissures run vertically, wide enough to get your fingers into, and there is something moving deep in one of them.
It is warmer than the room. Put a palm flat on it and you can feel it working, very slowly, somewhere behind the bark.
Names have been cut into it at about shoulder height. None of them are people you know. One of them is nearly yours.
name: the side of an enormous tree
says: I was here when this was a field. I will manage.
Do not lean on that part. It is newer than it looks.
The roof is mine. So is the floor, further down than you think.
